global_fields.name: num_sets

global_fields.name: budget_k

item_fields.name: set_id

global_fields.name: num_elements

global_fields.name: num_sets

global_fields.name: budget_k

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total size of the visitor universe: the number of distinct visitor identifiers that appear across all theme audiences. Used as the universe size for coverage bookkeeping (sanity-check / indexing), not the number the curator will necessarily reach.

global_fields.name: num_sets

global_fields.name: budget_k

item_fields.name: set_id

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for visitors expected to attend this theme. Identifiers may repeat across themes (indicating overlap); when evaluating a selection, count each visitor identifier only once toward total attendance.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct readers in the service area (the universe size). Each reader is counted once even if they can be reached from multiple stops.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential stops the bookmobile could visit. Each stop corresponds to a set listing which readers can be reached there.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of stops the driver may include on the route for this outing (the selection budget k). The chosen roster cannot exceed this number of stops.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate stop (for example a name or index). Use this ID to refer to that location when forming the roster of stops.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated reader identifiers representing the people reachable at this stop. If the same reader ID appears at multiple stops, they are the same person and count only once toward overall coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct community members considered across all fairs — i.e., the size of the attendee universe. This is the count of unique attendee IDs that may appear in the fair attendance lists.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of different community fairs available for sponsorship (the number of distinct fair entries provided).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of fairs the events team may sponsor (the k limit). You cannot select more fairs than this number.

item_fields.name: set_id

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of attendee identifiers (names or IDs) who visit that fair. When evaluating coverage, combine these lists for chosen fairs and count each unique attendee ID only once (duplicates across fairs do not increase coverage).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers mentioned across all proposed cleanup sites — the size of the volunteer universe we could possibly engage.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The count of distinct cleanup locations the team has proposed and can choose from.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of cleanup sites the leader may commit to coordinate (the bounded handful of locations the leader must lock in).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for a single cleanup site (a label the leader will use to refer to that location when selecting sites).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of volunteer identifiers who would attend that specific site if it runs; volunteers appearing at multiple sites are listed in each relevant site's entry but only count once toward total engagement.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct customers in the universe the owner considers (i.e., the size of the customer universe to be covered). This is used to check how many unique customers exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of different promotional bundles the shop could potentially offer (the number of available bundle options).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of promotional bundles the owner is allowed to run on the menu simultaneously — you cannot select more bundles than this cap.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific promotional bundle (used to reference that bundle when choosing the selection). Each bundle_id refers to one distinct offer and cannot be chosen more than once.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of customers who would be reached (interested in) that bundle. If this bundle is selected, all listed customer IDs are considered covered; a customer appearing in multiple bundles still counts only once toward total coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct passersby in the city planner's universe — i.e., the size of the population of people who might see notices (each person counted once).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate bulletin board locations on the closed list from which the planner may choose.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The hard upper bound on how many bulletin boards the planner is allowed to activate and use for posting notices.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or code) for a particular bulletin board location on the provided list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the distinct passersby who would see notices posted on this board — each identifier represents a single person in the planner's universe.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct households in the entire area (the universe of households). Used as a reference for the size of the problem — each household is an element that can be contacted.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available neighborhoods the charity can choose from. Each neighborhood corresponds to one candidate set of households that an outreach team can visit.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: Maximum number of outreach teams (i.e., the maximum number of neighborhoods) the charity can dispatch. The solution may select at most this many neighborhoods.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a neighborhood (e.g., a name or index). Used to refer to a specific neighborhood when selecting which ones to send teams to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of household identifiers belonging to this neighborhood. A household identifier may appear in multiple neighborhoods (overlap); when counting coverage, each household should be counted only once even if contacted from multiple selected neighborhoods.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct addresses in the rollout area (the size of the universe of addresses that could be covered by hubs).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate installation hubs available to choose from.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The firm limit on how many installation hubs the coordinator may select (maximum number of hubs allowed in the final plan).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate installation hub (e.g., hub code or name) that appears on the coordinator's list.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of addresses that this hub would serve (the set of addresses covered by that hub).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct students in the tutoring program's universe of possible attendees — i.e., the size of the student population that sessions could cover.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of different subject sessions available to choose from (each session is a fixed roster of students who would attend that session).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of sessions the program manager can offer given resource constraints; the chosen solution must not select more than this many sessions.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a particular subject session (e.g., subject name or code) that the manager can choose to run.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for students who would attend this session; when evaluating coverage, each student ID counts only once even if it appears in multiple session rosters.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct households in the problem universe — the count of unique household identifiers considered across all phone banks (the full universe the coordinator cares about).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available phone banks the coordinator could staff — the count of different phone-bank shifts/options from which a roster may be chosen.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of phone banks the coordinator may staff for this cycle — the roster size cap that the chosen selection of banks must not exceed.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single phone bank (a specific shift or call-team). Used to refer to that bank when building a roster.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated household identifiers that this phone bank will call. When multiple selected banks include the same household id, that household is counted only once toward the total reached.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct shoppers in the universe the buyer cares about (size of the shopper population considered for coverage).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate displays or placement options the merchandising team can choose from (each is a distinct display choice).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of displays the buyer is allowed to deploy; any chosen solution must select at most this many displays.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single display/placement option (used to reference that specific display in selections).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the shoppers that would be exposed if this display is deployed; shoppers may appear in multiple displays but count only once toward total coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct tourists the agent considers in town — the size of the universe of tourist identifiers that flyers can reach.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different flyer designs on the agent's shortlist (each design corresponds to one available set of tourists it can reach).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of different flyer designs the agent may choose to distribute. This selection limit (k) constrains how many flyers can be pushed to maximize distinct tourists reached.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific flyer design on the shortlist (used to refer to that flyer when selecting which designs to distribute).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the tourists who would receive this flyer if that design is distributed. Each identifier refers to a tourist in the universe; a tourist appearing in multiple lists still counts only once toward total coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct farmers in the district (the universe size). This is the count of unique farmer IDs/names that could be reached when the officer merges attendee lists from chosen demos.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of proposed demonstration plots available to choose from (the number of candidate sets the officer can select among).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: Coordination limit: the maximum number of demonstration plots the officer may run. The officer cannot select more demos than this number.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific demonstration plot (e.g., site code or name). Each demo is either run or not run.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers (names or IDs) of farmers who would likely attend this demo. When demos are selected, the officer will merge these lists, remove duplicates, and count unique farmers reached.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pupils across all candidate screening days — the size of the universe of students who appear on any listed day.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of possible screening days the nurse can choose from (i.e., how many distinct day-options/sets are available).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The hard cap on how many screening days the nurse may schedule; any chosen solution must include at most this many days.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a candidate screening day (for example a date or code) used to refer to that day's screening option.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of pupils who would attend that specific screening day. When combining chosen days, each pupil counts only once toward total coverage even if they appear on multiple days.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct testers in the universe the product lead cares about — i.e., the size of the tester pool across all previews (each tester counted once).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct preview ideas available for release that the product lead can choose from.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of previews the product lead may include in the bundle (the cap on how many previews can be released).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific preview idea (used to refer to that preview when selecting which ones to release).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of tester identifiers who will see this preview. When combining previews, each tester should be counted once even if they appear in multiple preview lists.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct neighborhoods in the service area that we care about reaching; this is the universe of neighborhoods to be covered by docks.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential docking locations under consideration (each is a candidate site you may choose to install a dock).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of docking locations you are allowed to select/install (the cap on chosen sites).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific candidate docking location (an ID you can use to refer to that site).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of neighborhood identifiers that would be served if that site is installed; each identifier names a neighborhood covered by this site (repeated coverage of the same neighborhood does not increase total reach).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct student interests in the universe — the full set of different interest categories you want to cover with clubs.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available after-school club options you can choose from (each option is a candidate club you might run).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The strict limit on how many clubs you may offer next term — the maximum number of club options you can select.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific club option (a short name or code you can use to refer to that particular club).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the student interests that this club appeals to or covers. When selecting clubs, each distinct interest counts once even if covered by multiple clubs.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct dietary preference categories we care about (e.g., vegan, gluten-free, nut-free). This is the size of the universe of dietary categories that specials can cover.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rotating specials available to choose from. Each special is a candidate menu item we could feature.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of specials we are allowed to feature at once. This is the selection limit (the 'k' in the maximum coverage problem).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier or name for a specific rotating special (e.g., 'Summer Salad', 'Tofu Bowl'). Use this to refer to that special when selecting the menu.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the dietary categories that this special satisfies (e.g., 'vegan gluten_free nut_free'). When evaluating choices, each listed category counts once even if multiple chosen specials cover it.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct element identifiers in the instance — i.e., the count of unique artists and genres that appear across all playlists. This is the universe whose coverage we aim to maximize.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate playlists available for selection (the total sets the editor can choose from).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of playlists the editor is allowed to highlight in this feature (k). The chosen playlists must not exceed this limit.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific playlist; used to refer to that playlist when selecting which ones to promote.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the artists and genres contained in this playlist. The coverage objective counts the union of these identifiers across selected playlists; repeated artists or genres across playlists only contribute once.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pollinator species in the universe under consideration — i.e., the size of the species pool that may be attracted across all crop varieties.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of crop varieties available for the farmer to choose from (the number of candidate sets of pollinator-attracting crops).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The hard cap on how many different crop varieties the farmer may plant; the maximum number of sets allowed in the selection.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct households in the campaign universe (the size of the merged household roll). This is the number of unique household identifiers that could be reached if all neighborhoods were combined — used to understand the full scope of coverage.

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct subjects/themes across the whole image pool. global_fields.name: num_elements

item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the learning objectives that this homework format practices. When counting coverage, objectives repeated across chosen formats are crossed off so each objective counts only once.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct listener interests in the universe — i.e., how many unique interest topics exist that the series could cover. Each interest is an identifier that themes may address.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of episode themes available to choose from for planning the series.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of episode themes you may schedule (the episode budget). You must pick at most this many themes to maximize distinct interest coverage.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this episode theme (the label used to refer to a theme when selecting or listing picks).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the listener interests this theme addresses. When evaluating a lineup, take the union of these ids across chosen themes and count each unique interest once (overlaps do not increase coverage).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct commuter routes and audience segments in the whole campaign universe. This is the size of the universe you’re trying to cover (i.e., the count of unique route/audience IDs that any billboard might reach).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: How many billboard site options are listed in total. Each site is a candidate location you could buy; this is the number of those candidate sites.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of billboard sites you are allowed to pick for the campaign. Your selected set of sites cannot exceed this cap.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or code) for a single billboard site option. Use this to refer to that specific location when choosing sites.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the route and audience IDs that would see the campaign if this billboard site is purchased. These IDs correspond to the universe of commuter routes/audience segments; when computing coverage, count each unique ID only once even if it appears from multiple sites.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct diner flavor preferences in the universe. This counts every unique preference that could be satisfied by at least one ingredient; it is the size of the preference universe the chef is trying to cover.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate ingredients the kitchen can choose from to feature as specials. Each available ingredient is a set that can satisfy one or more diner preferences.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of ingredients the chef may spotlight on the specials roster. The chosen featured ingredients must not exceed this cap.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single candidate featured ingredient (e.g., a name or numeric id). This labels the set corresponding to that ingredient.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the diner flavor preferences that this ingredient satisfies. When the ingredient is featured, each listed preference is considered covered (duplicate coverage across featured ingredients does not add extra).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct community needs considered (i.e., count of unique need identifiers in the universe the coordinator cares about).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different volunteer roles the coordinator can choose from (each role is a candidate to recruit).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of volunteer roles the coordinator may commit to recruiting (the cap on how many roles can be selected).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for a particular volunteer role (a label used to refer to this recruitable role).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the community needs that this role can address (each need the role covers).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct user complaints (unique issues) that exist in the backlog; this is the size of the universe of complaints we aim to address.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate features available to choose from; each feature is a potential item to build that can address one or more complaints.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: Maximum number of features the product manager can include in the next update (the slot limit). The chosen set of features must not exceed this number.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate feature (e.g., a feature name or index). Use this to reference which feature is selected.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the user complaints that this feature would address if built. When evaluating a selection, overlapping complaint identifiers among chosen features count only once toward the total addressed.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct product categories across the store universe that could be showcased (i.e., count of unique category identifiers available to cover).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available in-store demo stations you can choose from (each station is a candidate to run during the weekend).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of demo stations you are allowed to run simultaneously — the limit on how many stations may be selected.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific demo station (a unique label you can choose to run or skip).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of product categories that this demo station exposes shoppers to; when evaluating selections, merge these lists across chosen stations and count unique categories (do not double-count repeats).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct neighborhoods in the campaign area (i.e., size of the universe of neighborhoods we want to expose).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available community bulletin boards where we could post flyers (each board is one candidate set).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of bulletin boards we are allowed to post on for this outreach effort (the selection limit).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single community bulletin board (used to refer to that board when choosing where to post).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the neighborhoods that this bulletin board reaches or is associated with. When boards overlap, the same neighborhood identifier may appear in multiple boards but counts only once toward coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct households in the planning area (the universe of household identifiers that could be served by the clinics).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of potential pop-up clinic sites listed (each corresponds to one available clinic location you may choose).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of clinics the city can open given the budget constraint (the cap on how many sites you may select).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or label for this candidate clinic site (e.g., site code or name used to refer to the clinic).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of household identifiers (e.g., household IDs or address codes) that this clinic would serve; overlaps indicate households served by multiple clinics but should be counted only once when selecting sites.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct habitat types in the park that could be monitored (the size of the universe of habitats to cover).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of observation posts (towers) available as choices for staffing.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: Maximum number of observation posts the ranger crew can staff this week (the selection cap for chosen posts).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific observation post (a candidate tower the rangers can staff).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of habitat types visible from this post; if the post is staffed, these habitat types are considered monitored (overlaps with other posts count only once).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct streets in the city considered for delivery — the size of the universe of streets that routes may cover.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate local delivery routes available for the cafe to choose from.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of delivery routes the cafe owner is allowed to offer (the selection limit for routes).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific candidate delivery route (e.g., route number or name).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the streets that this route passes through; when routes are selected, each street contributes at most once to the cafe's total delivery coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct user needs (unique customer problems or use-cases) represented across all features — the size of the universe we aim to cover in the trial.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of different app features available to choose from for the trial; each is a candidate to include within the feature budget.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of features you are allowed to include in the trial — you cannot exceed this cap when selecting features to maximize covered user needs.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or code) for a specific app feature that can be selected for the trial.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the user needs that this feature addresses; when selecting features, these needs count toward the trial’s total coverage, with overlaps between features counted only once.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct households in the neighborhood (the size of the universe of households we want to reach).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of volunteers available to run signup tables (the number of candidate hosts you can choose from).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of volunteers you are allowed to select to run signup tables (the cap on hosts you can pick).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a volunteer (e.g., a name or ID number) used to refer to that candidate host.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of household identifiers that this volunteer can visit/reach if selected; households reached by multiple volunteers still count only once toward coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredient types present in the entire instance (the size of the ingredient universe across all stalls).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of supplier stalls available to choose from (the count of candidate vendors listed).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of stalls you are allowed to select for the market (the selection budget K limiting how many vendors get a stall).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific supplier stall (used to refer to that vendor when selecting stalls).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of ingredient-type identifiers that this stall offers; when evaluating a lineup, these contribute to the set of distinct ingredient types shoppers encounter.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct student concerns in the universe (count of unique concern types mentioned across all workshop options). This gives the scope of possible concerns but the goal is to maximize how many of these are covered by the chosen workshops.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available workshop sessions you can choose from — the number of different workshop options presented to the counselor.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of workshops you are allowed to run (the cap on selected sessions). You may choose up to this many workshops to maximize the count of distinct concerns addressed.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single workshop option (e.g., a name or numeric id) used to refer to that session when selecting the schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the student concerns this workshop addresses (for example: social_anxiety study_habits time_management). When workshops are selected, take the union of these concern identifiers and count each distinct concern once toward the objective.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct potential buyers considered across the whole campaign (i.e., the size of the universe of buyer IDs).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available open house locations that could be advertised in the email blast (each corresponds to one set of buyers reached).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of open house locations that may be included in the email blast (the cap on how many sets/locations you can choose).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific open house location (a label used to refer to that location when selecting which to advertise).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of potential buyers who would see the ad if this open house location is advertised (buyers may appear in multiple locations' lists due to audience overlap).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct facility areas (rooms, corridors, or zones) that appear in the instance — i.e., the size of the universe of areas we aim to observe.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of available camera positions that can be chosen from — each corresponds to one candidate camera location with a predefined coverage.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of cameras the supervisor is allowed to activate (the fixed limit N on selections). Solutions must select no more than this many camera positions.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a candidate camera position (e.g., 'cam1'). Used to refer to that camera when choosing which positions to activate.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of area identifiers that this camera observes (room and walkway IDs). When a camera is activated, all listed area IDs are considered covered; overlapping areas covered by multiple activated cameras count only once toward total coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct product categories available across all vendors (the size of the universe of categories you want to cover).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vendor booths available to choose from for the fair.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of vendor booths you can invite (the selection limit).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a vendor booth (e.g., booth number or vendor name) used to reference that vendor in selections.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for all product categories that this vendor sells; when a vendor is invited, these categories contribute to the fair's coverage (duplicate categories from multiple vendors count only once).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct apartment buildings in the service area (i.e., the size of the universe of buildings you want to serve).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate community drop points available to choose from (each is a possible location to maintain).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of drop points the delivery manager may select and maintain (the cap on how many sets you can pick).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific candidate drop point (used to refer to that location when selecting which points to keep).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of apartment buildings that can use this drop point — i.e., the buildings covered by this drop point (duplicates across drop points are allowed but count only once when measuring coverage).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct learner combinations (unique pairs or groups of learners/language needs) that could potentially be instructed. Each of these is an element the coordinator wants to cover at least once.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of different language-pair class options available to choose from. Each option is a possible class the coordinator can schedule and corresponds to a set covering certain learner combinations.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of class slots the coordinator can fill (how many language-pair classes may be selected). This is the selection budget limiting how many offerings can be chosen.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific language-pair class offering (e.g., a code or name for the class). Selecting this class uses one class slot and potentially covers multiple learner combinations.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the distinct learner combinations that this class supports (each token names a learner pairing or combination that would be taught if this class is offered). Overlap between classes is allowed but each unique combination is counted only once toward coverage.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct audience segments available across the whole campaign — i.e., the size of the universe of audience types that influencers can reach.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of influencer options you can choose from for the campaign.

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of influencer slots you may fill — the maximum number of influencers you are allowed to hire for the campaign.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this influencer (e.g., name or ID) used to reference which influencer is being selected.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of audience segments this influencer reaches. When scoring a selection, count the union of these segments across chosen influencers (do not double-count overlaps).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct neighborhoods in the city (the universe of neighborhoods we want the boxes to reach). Each neighborhood is counted once toward coverage regardless of how many boxes serve it.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible donation box locations you can choose from (each corresponds to a set of neighborhoods it attracts).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of donation boxes that may be placed — the upper limit on how many candidate locations you can select.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a candidate donation box location (each selected location must be distinct).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the neighborhoods served by this location — the neighborhoods from which donors are likely to come. Overlapping neighborhoods between locations do not add extra credit.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct practical skills across all proposed workshops — the size of the skill universe that sessions can cover (provided for reference).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate workshop sessions on the long list (each session is a selectable option you may choose to run).

global_fields.name: budget_k
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum number of workshop sessions you are allowed to schedule for the week (the cap on how many sessions you may pick).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for one workshop session (used to refer to that specific session when selecting the final schedule).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the practical skills taught in this session. When evaluating a selection of sessions, count each unique skill once even if it appears in multiple sessions.
